_comment: OBJECT REMOVAL, fully automatic. Name the thing you want gone in plain English (node 5), SAM 3.1 finds it, GrowMask pads the selection, and FLUX.1 Fill + the OneReward removal LoRA reconstructs what was behind it. No mask painting anywhere in this graph.
_notes: This is workflows 13 and 28 fused: SAM's text-prompted segmentation supplies the mask that FLUX Fill consumes. That chain is the whole point - every other removal tool makes you paint.

`noise_mask: true` here, unlike outpainting (workflow 28, false). For removal you WANT the masked region genuinely resampled from noise rather than nudged, otherwise a ghost of the original object survives as a smudge.

GROW THE MASK. SAM returns a tight silhouette, and a tight mask leaves the object's contact shadow, reflection and colour-bleed behind - which reads worse than leaving the object in. `GrowMask` at 24 px plus `blur_radius` handles ordinary cases; go to 40+ for anything glossy or strongly shadowed. This is the single most common reason a removal looks bad.

`removal_timestep_alpha-2-1740.safetensors` (node 4) is a small LoRA specifically trained for removal - it biases the model toward reconstructing plausible BACKGROUND rather than inventing a replacement object. Without it, FLUX Fill will cheerfully paint a different watch where the old one was.

MEASURED RESULT: THIS FAILED on the shipped example, twice, and the failure is worth more than a success would be. Asked to remove a wristwatch from a product shot, it produced a woven rope ring, then a carved stone ring - both times a NEW object occupying the watch's silhouette. The mask was verified correct (a clean solid blob over the watch), and both prompt conventions were tried: describing the empty surface, and the template's instruction form ('Remove the wristwatch.'). Neither helped.

WHY it fails here, and when to expect it: the mask is ~35% of the frame, dead centre, on a plinth-like slab. Everything about that composition says 'an object belongs here', so the model fills the hole with an object whose silhouette matches. Removal works well on a SMALL object inside a CONTEXTFUL scene, where surrounding pixels tell the model what the background should be. It works badly on the subject of a product shot, because there is no background to infer - the object IS the picture. For that case, re-generate the plate empty rather than removing.

Prompt convention, for the record: the OneReward template uses an instruction ('Remove the girl's hat'), not a description of the desired background. Use the instruction form. It was not sufficient here, but it is the correct convention.
FluxGuidance 30 and cfg 1.0, same as workflow 28 - the Fill model's trained range.
Verify with the saved mask output (node 12). If the removal looks wrong, look at the mask before touching anything else - it is nearly always the mask.

inputs.text: An empty wet black slate slab on a dark surface, scattered water droplets across the stone, soft studio light, nothing resting on it.
